source_rows.role: option score, long-range effect, and bounded distribution
source_rows.finding: CBO/JCT publish the ten-year deficit effect, higher scheduled benefits, three-year depletion delay under the vintage baseline, and retirement tax-and-benefit effects by household earnings quintile and birth cohort.
The 2026 report projects combined reserve depletion in 2034, 83 percent payable then, and a 4.42 percent-of-taxable-payroll 75-year deficit.
The 2026 contribution and benefit base is $184,500 and the combined employee-employer OASDI rate is 12.4 percent.
The taxable ratio was 83.3 percent in 2023 and 2024 and is projected to converge to 82.5 percent by 2035 under intermediate assumptions.
SSA estimates a phased 2026-2035 90-percent provision with benefit credit, but it is not the immediate CBO alternative or a 2026 Trustees rescore.

gate_rows.evidence: CBO/JCT define the immediate 90-percent alternative and publish annual deficit effects.
SSA supplies the 2026 trust-fund, $184,500 base, 12.4-percent rate, and 83.3-percent latest taxable-ratio context.
CBO publishes retirement benefit and lifetime payroll-tax effects for three birth cohorts and household-earnings quintiles.
Statutory shares and CBO household results do not identify compensation shifting, labor response, employer incidence, or self-employed administration.
The bounded retired-worker table does not close survivor, disability, family, poverty, or vulnerable-population outcomes.
No current implementation plan costs payroll systems, benefit records, avoidance, compliance, or transition.
The official deficit score includes an income-tax offset, but no TAXLANE joint tax-unit allocation with REV is complete.
The vintage result improves actuarial balance by 0.9 percent of payroll and delays depletion three years but does not achieve full solvency or use the 2026 Trustees baseline.
